title: Warrior
summary: Heavy iron, short answers, and bad knees in the rain.
infobox: Rusty Sword, Wooden Buckler, Padded Jerkin, Leather Boots, Healing Draught

p: A veteran border-guard who treats battlefields like bad weather—something to be endured behind good oak and thick plate. Built to hold choke points, break shield walls, and survive mistakes that would fold lesser mercenaries.
Hold narrow bridges and doorways behind heavy plate and shield walls, interrupting enemy casters while mercenaries flank.
Front-loaded HP and Strength let warriors anchor chokes from level 1; mid-game points shift toward Vitality and Mind for resistance caps.

Twelve years on the Thornwick border taught him two useful habits: check your cinch-straps before dawn, and never volunteer for a parade. He survived three reorganizations of the provincial levy simply by being too stubborn to die and too reliable to dismiss.

When the salt-tax riots turned into full-scale siege warfare, his company was paid in promissory notes stamped by clerks who had already fled south. He kept the shield, pawned the ceremonial sash, and started taking contracts where the silver was weighed upfront.
He does not care who sits on the Obsidian Throne or why the wells went dry. Someone paid to have the road cleared, and he intends to collect before his joints lock up for good.

She spent seven years commanding sapper crews in the northern quarries before a magistrate blamed her for a collapsed watchtower she had warned him not to load with siege stone. They stripped her commission and let her keep the breastplate she had personally riveted.

Without a guild seal, she sold her weight in steel to merchant caravans crossing contested fords. She learned quickly that men underestimating a woman in heavy mail only make that mistake once per limb.
She marches south not for honor, but because shattered fortresses pay better than intact ones—and Thornvael looks overdue for a thorough inspection.

title: Archer
summary: Good eyes, dry wit, and zero interest in melee.
infobox: Ash Shortbow, Leather Cap, Padded Jerkin, Leather Gloves, Healing Draught

p: A sharp-tongued reconnaissance hunter who prefers solving problems from sixty paces behind cover. Excels at picking off high-value targets, crippling advancing lines, and reminding heavy infantry how loud they breathe.
Control sightlines from ridges and flanks, crippling advancing brutes with snares and sniping enemy hexers before lines collide.
High Dexterity scales accuracy and critical strikes rapidly through Act II; invest in Mind by Act III to sustain volley cooldowns.
She learned her trade poaching crown deer in the border woods, where getting caught meant losing a thumb and missing a shot meant going hungry. Both lessons stuck remarkably well.

After three winters guiding tax assessors through marshland—and occasionally leaving the rude ones on the wrong side of a peat bog—she discovered that military scouting paid twice as much for half the conversation.
She follows the campaign south mostly out of professional curiosity: someone keeps building bigger walls, and she enjoys finding the drafty gaps in all of them.

For nine years he manned a wooden watch-platform above the Redmarsh salt-roads, collecting bridge tolls with a yew longbow and a slate of charcoal tallies. Nobody ever argued the tariff twice when his arrow landed three inches from their boot.
When bandit companies burned the toll-posts and conscripted the clerks, he took his quiver into the reeds and spent two autumns thinning their officers one dusk at a time.
He joined the southward march because wild game has grown scarce near the ash-drifts, and bounty silver buys better goose-feathers than marsh-reed fletching.

title: Mage
summary: Precise equations, volatile gestures, and mild dread.
infobox: Oak Staff, Scholar Hat, Cloth Robe, Sandals, Mana Draught

p: A methodical arcana-scholar who views magic not as miracle, but as hazardous thermodynamics. Capable of unraveling formations from afar, provided nothing interrupts the third syllable of the invocation.
Shape the battlefield with timed AoE bursts, frost slows, and wards while keeping hired shield-bearers between robes and blades.
Starts fragile with tight mana pools, scaling sharply once Mind unlocks multi-target elemental combos and high-tier spell tomes.

Expelled from the Capital Collegium for publishing a monograph proving that half the state liturgy consisted of corrupted plumbing diagrams, he retreated to the provinces with three trunks of annotated notebooks.
Field work in Thornvael has been deeply inconvenient: rain warps vellum, blood ruins chalk circles, and mercenaries routinely stand inside blast radii despite explicit verbal warnings.
He presses onward toward the Obsidian Core because the ambient ley-drift violates every known conservation law—and leaving an unmeasured anomaly behind would keep him awake for years.
Precise equations, volatile gestures, and mild dread.

Trained in the Thornwick Mint to test ore purity with galvanic arcs, she left after discovering the treasury was quietly shaving silver from soldiers' pay while blaming her instruments for the variance.
She took her copper-wound focus rod on the road and quickly learned that bandit captains conduct lightning even better than counterfeit coins.
She follows the campaign toward Crown and Ember because the volcanic vents are distorting regional ley-currents—and someone needs to shut the valve before the whole continent shorts out.

title: Necromancer
summary: Unpaid debts, dry ink, and borrowed sinew.
infobox: Willow Wand, Apprentice Circlet, Cloth Robe, Bone Ring, Mana Draught

p: A dour mortuary clerk who treats death not as tragedy or triumph, but as an unsettled ledger. Calls up indentured bone and lingering echoes to collect the labor the living never finished.
Audit the battlefield through patient attrition—bind fallen foes as bone shields, compound curses on elites, and siphon vigor.
Steady hybrid scaling balances Mind for minion capacity and curses with Vitality to survive blood-tithes and attrition fights.
Unpaid debts, dry ink, and borrowed sinew.

For fourteen years he kept the pauper-rolls in Thornwick's lower parish, recording unpaid tax liens that outlived their debtors by three generations. One winter, when the bailiffs demanded he collect from a flooded graveyard, he learned how to summon the signatories directly.

Excommunicated for 'improper probate procedure,' he packed his bone-awl, three ledgers of uncollected vows, and a brass scale, taking his practice to the border wars where fresh arrears accumulate hourly.
He marches toward Crown and Ember because the Anchor Seals have frozen thousands of ancient oaths in limbo—and someone has to audit the books before the interest crushes the realm.
Quiet vows, cold scales, and servants who never complain.
Raised in a coastal scriptorium that witnessed deathbed wills for sailors and smugglers, she learned early that a promise spoken over salt and bone outlasts the lungs that uttered it.

When corrupt magistrates began forging wills to seize widows' cottages, she invoked the dead testators in open court to cross-examine the bailiffs. She was thanked with a warrant for heresy and a head start to the border.
She travels south because the war has left thousands of sworn protectors unburied and un-released—and until their contracts are fulfilled, none of them can rest.
A battle-hardened defender of Thornwick in tempered gothic plate.
A mercenary duelist and ranger wielding twin curved daggers.
An ordained fire scholar from the Citadel of Embers.
Keeper of ancient tide-runes who freezes charging hordes.
